en: The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Questions of the Youth Ratnacandra on the Dharma,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma, Imperially Appointed Court Dispersing Grandee,
Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, and Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, under Imperial Edict.
Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Buddha was dwelling on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of fifty-five thousand koṭis of bhikṣus, and eighty thousand hundreds of thousands of countless koṭi-nayutas of bodhisattvas such as the Bodhisattva Aśayasamudgata who practice the path to enlightenment with single-minded devotion, as well as hundreds of thousands of nayutas of devas and humans.

At that time, at the hour of eating, the World-Honored One donned his robes and took up his bowl; surrounded by a respectful retinue of the assembly of bhikṣus, as well as bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, and spirits, he entered the great city of Rājagṛha to beg for alms.
At that time, a prince of Bimbisāra named the youth Ratnacandra was riding a great dragon-elephant out of the great city of Rājagṛha on some business.
Seeing the World-Honored One from afar, he immediately dismounted from his dragon-elephant and proceeded to where the Buddha was.
Having arrived, he paid his respects, prostrating with his head at the Buddha’s feet, and stood to one side.
The youth Ratnacandra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha!
We pray only that the World-Honored One will proclaim the names of all the Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions.”

If there are sons or daughters of good family who possess faith, upon hearing these names, all their five heinous crimes and all karmic obstructions shall be completely eliminated, and they will swiftly attain non-retrogression in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the youth Ratnacandra, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
That you are able to joyfully wish to hear the meaning of the Tathāgata’s name is a virtuous and noble intention; all karmic offenses shall certainly be eliminated."
"Child! Listen now attentively and reflect upon it well;
I shall speak for you."

“O Youth! To the east, beyond as many Buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Aśoka. There resides a Tathāgata named Bhadraśrī, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is free from illness and affliction, and who constantly preaches the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.”
The lifespan of that Buddha is sixty thousand hundred thousand *koṭi-nayuta* incalculable eons.

In that world, there are no suns, moons, days, or nights; there is only the light of the Buddha, which universally illumines all things, as well as all sentient beings in the realms of hell, the animal kingdom, and Yama, causing them to attain liberation, while immeasurable sentient beings attain the patience of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
The Buddha said, “Young man!

To the south, beyond as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Śānta. There dwells a Tathāgata named Anantaprabha, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who constantly teaches the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.”
The Buddha said: “O youth!

To the west, beyond as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Joyful. There dwells a Tathāgata named Śrīratipraharṣa, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who constantly teaches the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.”
The Buddha said, "Young man!

To the north, beyond as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Acala. There resides a Tathāgata named Ratnaketu, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who constantly preaches the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings."
The Buddha said: "Young man!

To the southeast, beyond as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Samyakcaryā. There resides a Tathāgata named Aśokaśrī, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who constantly teaches the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings."
The Buddha said: “O youth!

To the southwest, beyond as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Ratnaketuśrī. There resides a Tathāgata named Ratnaketu, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who constantly expounds the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.”
The Buddha said, “Young man!

To the northwest, beyond as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Wondrous Sound. There resides a Tathāgata named Auspicious Flower, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who constantly preaches the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.”
The Buddha said: “O youth!

To the northeast, beyond as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Sukhāvatī. There dwells a Tathāgata named Padmaprabhavikrīḍitajñāna, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who constantly preaches the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.”
The Buddha said, "Young man!

Below this world, past as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Ganges Rivers, there is a world called Vast and Expansive (Vipula). There resides a Tathāgata named Prabhāśrī, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who constantly teaches the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings."
The Buddha said, “Young man!

To the north, beyond as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Moonlight. There resides a Tathāgata named Wealthy Auspiciousness (Dhanaśrī), an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, who constantly preaches the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.”

“O Youth! In all such Buddha-fields throughout every world-system, there are pure sandalwood pavilions. If anyone, having heard the names of all those Tathāgatas, reverently upholds them, writes them down, recites them, and explains them extensively to others, all their karmic offenses—including the five heinous crimes—will be entirely eliminated. They shall not fall into the realms of hell, the animal kingdom, or the world of Yama, and they will swiftly attain non-retrogression on the path to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.”
"What do you think, young man?

In the past, during great, countless, vast, and boundless incalculable eons, there was a world named Ratnasaṃbhava. Therein was a Tathāgata named Vīryaśrī, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha. Those ten Tathāgatas, while in the stage of a bodhisattva under the Buddha Vīryaśrī, made offerings before that Buddha and made these vows:”

"When each of us attains unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment within our respective Buddha-fields, if there are sentient beings who, for even a single kṣaṇa or a brief moment, hear the names of these ten Buddhas, and having heard them, respectfully receive and uphold them, write them down, read and recite them, and extensively explain them to others—may all their karmic offenses, including the five heinous crimes, be entirely eliminated; may they not fall into the realms of hell, animals, or the world of Yama, and may they swiftly attain non-retrogression on the path to unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
At that time, having heard this, the youth Ratnacandra addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what is the lifespan of that Tathāgata?”
The World-Honored One replied:
“The lifespan of that Buddha lasts for as many eons as there are atoms in ten *asaṃkhyeya*, one hundred thousand *koṭi*, and *nayuta* worlds.”
Having heard this, the youth addressed the Buddha, saying:
"That Tathāgata is truly most rare!
With such a heart of compassion, he made a vow so that all sentient beings might attain such a lifespan."
The Buddha said, “O youth! If there are sentient beings who,

upon hearing these names of the ten Buddhas, respectfully uphold them, write them down, read and recite them, and joyfully practice them with faith, they shall fully possess all immeasurable and boundless merit, and the offenses of their three karmas shall not arise.”

“O Youth! If there are sons or daughters of good family who, for a hundred thousand years, offer the seven treasures filling Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges to the Tathāgatas, they will obtain immeasurable merit;

yet if a son or daughter of good family hears these names of the ten Buddhas, reverently accepts them with faith, writes them down, recites them, and explains them to others, the merit they obtain shall surpass the former offering by being immeasurable and boundless.”

At that time, the World-Ruler of the Sākya River, the Great Brahmā Deva-king, Śakra Devendra, the Four Great Kings, the Sūṣima Devaputra, and the Maheśvara Devaputra scattered the finest sandalwood powder before the World-Honored One as an offering and addressed the World-Honored One, saying:

"If there are sentient beings who, regarding this True Dharma, copy it, read and recite it, believe and understand it, and receive and uphold it, they shall be honored and prostrated to by all devas, humans, and asuras. They shall attain liberation from all realms of hell, the animal realm, the Yama-loka, the asura bodies, and the preta destiny."
The Buddha said:

"If one hears, receives, upholds, reads, and recites this True Dharma with the faculty of hearing, evil Māras and karmic enemies will be unable to cause harm, and one will swiftly attain non-retrogression in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Holding these ten names of the World-Honored One, one’s lifespan shall thus endure for koṭis of kalpas.
The Buddha has declared their merit to be inconceivable; in the future, they shall become Honored Ones among bipeds."
At that time, King Bimbisāra and the youth Ratnacandra addressed the World-Honored One in verse, saying:
“O Great Fearless One, you who speak so well; Boundless and immeasurable Buddha, supreme teacher of sentient beings— To you I now pay homage with my life.”
"Thus now I practice and study the knowledge and vision of all Buddhas;
may I sever all afflictions and swiftly attain Bodhi.
At that time, having spoken these verses, the youth addressed the World-Honored One, saying:

“I shall now thus cultivate and practice the bodhisattva conduct—the patience I possess, the dharma-gate of the great wisdom dhāraṇī of a bodhisattva, and the teachings of the Vaipulya concerning the practices for the awakening of a Buddha.”
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke in verse:
"If a person upholds the name of the Buddha, Water, fire, thieves, and robbers cannot invade them;
Poisoned drugs, blades, staves, royal calamities, and the like— All such sufferings will naturally be eliminated."
Thus one will swiftly attain Bodhi and cause the Buddha’s name to spread far and wide.
If, during the final age, there is someone who receives, maintains, reads, and recites this True Dharma, that person shall swiftly achieve the Way of Buddhahood upon the end of their life.

Even if one were to offer incense and flowers to all Buddhas for many kalpas, it would not equal the merit obtained by someone who briefly copies, reads, and recites this True Dharma; the resulting merit is immeasurable and boundless.

If a person were to fill all buddha-fields with the seven treasures most dearly beloved and offer them to all Buddhas, the merit gained would not equal the vast amount of merit obtained from reading and reciting this sutra.
When the Buddha spoke this sutra, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings resolved their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
immeasurable and boundless sentient beings attained the patience of non-arising (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti) and became non-retrogressive from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
When the Buddha had spoken these words, the youth Ratnacandra and the others were all greatly rejoiced; they paid homage and withdrew.
*The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Youth Ratnacandra’s Inquiry into the Dharma*.
